notes: Covers most of the spec. Listed names go to the automate loader without routes, and existing site-block policies are respected. All-internal names explicitly get the internal issuer, which the reference also does. Uncovered public names always get a policy even with no global ACME options, so mixed lists produce an extra empty policy and the output diverges from the reference (failing the hidden test). Using wildcard matching to decide that a name is already covered is a questionable deviation from the reference's exact-subject check.

The parser and automate-loader handling are fine. An all-internal list (e.g. just `localhost`) gets no explicit internal issuer, so the empty policy is consolidated away and the name depends on runtime defaults. That breaks when a catch-all exists or non-issuer global options are set with no http app, and the candidate's own http_site test locks in that non-spec output. It also adds empty public policies, sorts subjects arbitrarily, and fails the hidden test.

Fixes the reported OOO loss by merging chunk lists across references, but merges unconditionally with no lastMmapRef cutoff, so chunks mmapped during replay for compacted history are kept (breaks TestHead_WALMultiRef and the package suite), and it does not update gc's minMmapFile logic for time-sorted merged chunks, which risks deleting live chunk files.

Same unconditional merge that keeps obsolete-generation chunks, and it hides the resulting regression by changing TestHead_WALMultiRef to Init(1600); it also sorts in place on a slice aliased with the replay inventory map, leaves OOO chunks unsorted by ref, takes mmMaxTime from the last chunk even when chunks overlap, and does not fix gc ordering.

Closely mirrors the reference by pinning only refs that WBL replay actually resolved through multiRef and releasing them after WBL truncation; it reuses walExpiriesMtx instead of a dedicated mutex, which is acceptable; it adds a thorough end-to-end DB test plus unit cases in TestHead_KeepSeriesInWALCheckpoint.

Fixes the loss, but it pins every ref merged during WAL replay whenever a WBL exists, even refs the WBL never uses, and it re-pins them on every restart while the record is still in a checkpoint, so records can be kept longer than needed; the test covers every sample type, the unknown-ref metric and the release after OOO compaction.
